instructions: Edit this file to update every measured figure on the site. Do not add a number unless it is in the resume or in a committed result file in the project's repository. The home page, case studies, and tables all read from here. Each project has one headline stat (headline.stat), three short facts (factIds), and a short caveat. Search this file for the old value and update every place it appears, including caveat text.

projects.title: Orbit
projects.purpose: Orbit Code: a planner, a coder, a test runner, and a reviewer. The reviewer can refuse a patch that fails the hidden tests or edits the tests.
projects.proves: A reviewer can refuse a patch. The team passed 29 of 32 frozen tasks and a single agent passed 27. No interval is in the file, so that gap is not an improvement.
projects.summary: Orbit Code, code-eval-v2, claude-haiku-5-5, scored once: team with reviewer 29 of 32, single agent 27 of 32. The archive has no paired interval. Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, harness v3, scored once: fine-tuned schema-valid rate 0.333 to 0.764, 95% interval above zero; task success interval includes zero.
projects.caveat: code-eval-v2, claude-haiku-5-5, 32 frozen tasks, scored once: team with reviewer passed 29 of 32, single agent passed 27 of 32. The measured files have no paired interval, so that gap is not an improvement. Reviewer refusals were 1 of 32 on the team run and 2 of 32 on the single-agent run. On the team run, mf-span and zip-safe failed the hidden test and were not refused. On the single-agent run, mf-span, mf-csv, and zip-safe failed and were not refused. Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, harness v3, frozen 12-task test, scored once: schema-valid rate 0.333 on the base team to 0.764 with the fine-tuned adapter (95% interval on the difference 0.264 to 0.607, above zero). Task success 2 of 12 to 4 of 12 (interval −0.167 to 0.500, includes zero), so task success is not an improvement. The fine-tuned team refused 1 of 2 traps. The distilled team passed 2 of 12, schema-valid 0.448; against the base team that schema-valid interval is −0.064 to 0.278 and includes zero. The result files name the model and the adapters. They do not name the GPU. Boardroom and the incident commander are scripted demos, not scores.

projects.title: Time-series foundation model
projects.summary: A decoder-only transformer pretrained from scratch in PyTorch. On the test split, patch_s2, one seed, 97 configurations: CRPS 0.688× upstream AutoARIMA, 95% CI [0.624, 0.757], better. Validation CRPS was 0.605× Seasonal Naive.
projects.caveat: patch_s2 on the test split, one seed, 97 configurations: CRPS 0.688× upstream AutoARIMA, 95% CI [0.624, 0.757], better. Its validation CRPS was 0.605× Seasonal Naive, 16 configurations, one seed. A smaller CPU model (833,440 parameters, 3 seeds, 97 configurations) was scored once on the test split: CRPS 1.109× Seasonal Naive, no detectable difference, and 1.217× AutoARIMA, worse.

projects.title: World Shock Lab
projects.summary: Event studies of Federal Reserve, Bank of Canada, and OPEC surprises across global assets, with a pre-registered test of whether machine learning adds anything, and a scenario tool published before each decision.
projects.caveat: Machine learning did not beat the linear model on the average move in either pre-registered study. Quantile boosting won only on 5% tail pinball loss. None of 80 regime tests survived false-discovery control.

projects.title: ATLAS
projects.purpose: An economic research terminal that traces how a cost shock travels through the world's production networks.
projects.summary: Real country data, seven OECD production tables, a PyTorch scenario solver and saved neural checkpoints, served by one local FastAPI process with a React interface. Every result is labelled as observed, hypothetical or learned.
projects.caveat: A local research terminal, not a hosted service. In the graph experiment, ridge regression beat every neural and graph model on the one held-out year. Latencies are warm requests on one machine.
